hypothesis: The page trim display is driven by one of the two listeners of the knob property - so calling that listener alone repaints the trim
test: Call listener 0 then listener 1 slot 0x28 with (value target) from the button hook and diff the framebuffer
notes: listener 1 alone changes 0 px; listener 0 crashes the app. Both listeners share one call slot 0xaaaaacccd640

hypothesis: Calling only the page listener will not crash - the crash comes from the broadcaster's other work
test: Same test: check the pid after the listener call
notes: listener 0 crashed on its own too

hypothesis: The property lookup returned a class prototype inside the image instead of the live heap property
test: Exclude image addresses from prop_of_param and re-run the poke
notes: fixed: prop_of_param now skips base..base+0x9000000; poke then found heap properties and stopped crashing

hypothesis: The CC handler and the state-sync function use the same control base
notes: handler uses base+0x1ac0 (mov x7 0x1ac0); sync function at 0x2822400 uses x19+0x18b8/1910/1968/... stride 0x58 - i.e. +0x1ac8. With 0x1ac8 the handler finds no owner object at all

hypothesis: The model the page draws from is the object the sync function reads at x20+0x1908 etc
test: Locate the sync function entry and its x20 argument
notes: 0x2822474 bl 0x13bb930 after ldr s0 [x20+0x1960]; the properties are x19+0x18b8+0x58*k and the model fields are x20+0x1908+0x58*k - exactly property+0x50

hypothesis: The sync function is the model->UI bridge the page uses
test: Hook 0x2822260 and read its two arguments at the trim offsets
notes: the two arguments are stack temporaries 0x3d30 apart that grow per call - this is the save/serialize path not the load path

hypothesis: Recovering from the replay's fault with siglongjmp keeps the app alive
test: Wrap the replay in sigsetjmp and longjmp from the SIGSEGV handler
notes: the fault happens after the call returns (asynchronously) so no recovery point is active; no longjmp was taken

hypothesis: Both controls injected in one UI turn is what leaves the app in a state it dies on
test: Inject one control per paint call (step 1 / step 2)
notes: splitting removes the crash (pid stable) but the page no longer updates (HAND vs AUTO 4817 px); the one-shot version is pixel-identical but crashes about a second later

hypothesis: Delivering the two controls in one UI turn updates the model and the page
test: run the one-turn replay then re-select the pad and diff vs the hand reference
notes: page becomes pixel-identical (HAND vs AUTO 0 px) - the model really is updated by that path

hypothesis: The split (one control per paint) also updates the model, so a reload would show it
test: split replay then re-select the pad and diff
notes: FULL vs AUTO 0 px - the split updates nothing; only the one-turn replay does

hypothesis: The crash is a stack overflow from re-entrancy through the paint hook
test: fault sp is 0xfffffffff3d0 which is below every mapping (vsyscall page boundary)
notes: sp at the fault is not in any real stack; the fault registers could not be captured in the run that survived

hypothesis: The one-turn replay is reproducible - it always updates the model
test: Repeat the one-turn replay on a fresh app twice and diff against the hand reference
notes: one run gave HAND vs AUTO 0 px before a crash; a fresh run with the same code gave 4817 px and no crash. Outcome varies between runs

hypothesis: The learned properties are being used by the commit
test: Read the props log during a trim
notes: props 0xffffe4f0c718/0xffffe4f0c770 with cur -1 then 0.0000/0.8268 - the learned pair is found and the injection runs

hypothesis: The page shades the trimmed-out region grey (27 27 30) rather than black
test: Sample the pixel runs across the waveform at y=120 for a hand-set trim
notes: hand-set K2=105 gives the grey run at x=257..304; drawing black over 253..305 was wrong

hypothesis: Drawing the same shading makes the autotrim page match a hand trim
test: Diff the framedump after drawing grey shading + edges against the hand-set reference
notes: HAND vs AUTO dropped from 5078 px to 1090 px (the remainder is our 1 px edge line and the 0.5% position difference); FULL vs AUTO is 5197 px so the trim is clearly visible

hypothesis: The bottom area shows the knob's trim value and is missing after autotrim
test: Sample the non-background pixels in y226..238 for K2 = 0 / 105 / 127
notes: the only non-background pixels are static at x=15..20 and x=311..314 for all three values; the 52 px hand-vs-full difference is the knob focus highlight, not a value indicator

hypothesis: The app's slider widget drives the visible Start/End bars
test: Write slider+0x1b4 for the mapped slider and diff the bottom band
notes: write lands ('slider 0xffffe4a2ffe8 -> 82.54%') but the band does not change
